🎉 New A.I. Agent Runs On A Single GPU; Humanity Briefly Remembers What 'One' Means

MENLO PARK — reported from a refreshingly small server

MODELS — Meta released a 30-billion-parameter AI agent that runs on a single GPU — a stunning act of restraint in an industry whose previous strategy was "acquire every graphics card on Earth, and then ask around for more."

"You can run it on one machine," an engineer said, to a room that gasped as though he'd described witchcraft. Analysts hailed the model as proof that AI can, in fact, be efficient — a discovery the industry will now celebrate by immediately building a version that needs nine thousand GPUs.

📱 Google To Launch Pixel 11 With A Comedian Host; Phone Reportedly Also Funny, Unintentionally

NEW YORK — reported from the third row of a product keynote

GADGETS — Google confirmed its Made by Google event, where the Pixel 11 family will headline a show hosted by a famous comedian and stuffed with entertainment — because nothing says "buy this rectangle" quite like a professional trying to make a spec sheet land.

"It's going to be a whole experience," Google promised, of an event where the jokes are scripted and the battery life is aspirational. Attendees are advised to laugh at the bezels and hold their applause for the price reveal.

🖱️ This Month's Gadgets Include A Folding Mouse; Society Quietly Asks Which Problem This Solves

THE SHOWROOM — reported from a deeply confusing nightstand

GADGETS — August's gadget lineup features a folding mouse, a bedside unit that replaces three devices, and a dual-screen E-Ink tablet — a triumphant set of answers to questions absolutely no one asked, delivered with total confidence.

"It folds!" the folding mouse's makers announced, of a product solving the ancient human struggle of a mouse being slightly too mouse-sized. Reviewers admit it is clever, pointless, and exactly the kind of thing you will own within a year and be unable to explain to guests.

🔊 Google Releases A New Smart Speaker After Six Years; It Has A Lot Of Listening To Catch Up On

YOUR LIVING ROOM — reported quietly, just in case

SMART HOME — For the first time in six years, Google unveiled a new smart speaker — returning to the living room refreshed, redesigned, and presumably very eager to resume hearing absolutely everything you say.

"It's smarter than ever," the company said of a device rejoining a market it left back when "AI assistant" still mostly meant "thing that sets a timer for the wrong hour." The speaker can reportedly now hold a real conversation, which is either delightful or the last thing you want from an object that is always on.

💵 Intel Raises $15 Billion To Stay In The A.I. Race; Money Immediately Turns Into Heat

SANTA CLARA — filed from a very warm balance sheet

MARKETS — Intel raised a fresh $15 billion to keep pace in the intensifying AI race — a sum that, at the going exchange rate, converts to roughly one and a half data centers and one truly heroic electricity bill.

"We're all in," the company said, of an industry where "competing" now means setting fifteen billion dollars gently on fire in a temperature-controlled room and hoping it emerges as a chip. Investors nodded, having long ago accepted that in AI, the budget is the product.
